title: Guide / EPG button
answer: Press the remote's Guide or EPG button from a screen in your profile to open the live guide on the playing channel. It also works from full screen and supports the Formuler EPG button. In Sports Mode it opens the in-page Live TV panel and keeps the current game playing until you choose another channel. On regular TV home it opens the TV tab and guide. The splash and profile selector keep their normal controls.

title: Watch catch-up TV
answer: On a channel where your provider offers catch-up, open the Timeline guide and press Left to browse earlier programmes. Available replays have a gold ↺ mark. OK on a past programme starts the preview; OK again on that programme opens it full screen. Older hours without programme names appear as Catch-up HH:MM blocks and can also be played. How far back you can watch depends on your provider's retention window.
controls: Android · Timeline · ← into the past · OK twice

title: Back to now in the guide
answer: When browsing a different time in the Timeline guide, Back returns the guide to now; the gold Now button does the same. This only moves the guide: a replay keeps playing. Fast-forward does not return to live from the guide. To change playback back to live, open the replay full screen and use its gold LIVE button, or Fast-forward to the end of the replay. Back from full screen returns to the guide while the replay continues.
controls: In the guide: Back or the gold Now button

title: Catch-up not working
answer: If replay channels or past programmes are missing after updating, run Update Content and update your playlists, then Update EPG Now once. Catch-up is available on Android TV, Fire TV and Android phones; Windows support is not available yet. Your provider must offer catch-up for that channel. The provider decides how many days are available; guide data may cover fewer hours, with older hours shown as Catch-up HH:MM blocks. Refreshing cannot add replay support to a channel your provider does not support.
controls: Update Content → update playlists · Settings → Playlists & guide → EPG → Update EPG Now

title: Preview, then full screen
answer: The first OK plays the channel in the preview box; OK again opens it full screen.

title: Search channels
answer: Open Search from the side menu and enter the channel name. Matching channels appear in the Live TV row. Move to a channel and press OK to play it. Search also shows matching movies, TV shows and Media Hub titles in separate rows.
controls: Search (magnifying glass) in the side menu

title: Channel menu
answer: Add to / Remove from Favourites, Hide this channel, Move Up / Down (your own order inside the group or Favourites), Move to group…, Remove from a group, and Record on Android. To reorder Favourites in the list or Timeline guide, hold OK on a channel, choose Move Up / Down, use ↑ / ↓, then OK or Back to finish. Each viewer's order is saved across playlists and takes priority over the default playlist or A-Z order. Clear the guide's search filter before moving a channel.

title: Sort live groups
answer: The filter icon offers Provider order, Name A–Z and Name Z–A. Each playlist stays together; your own groups sort separately. The choice is remembered on this device. Manual Move Up / Down or Move to Top restores the stored order. Favourites channel order stays as you arranged it.

title: Group menu
answer: Add to Favourites, Hide Group, Move Up / Down, Move to Top, and New group… to start your own group.

title: Your group's menu
answer: Move Up / Down, Move to Top, New group…, Delete. Your groups sit under Favourites and History and mix channels from every playlist.
controls: Hold OK on your own group

title: Clear this tab's favourites
answer: Asks first. Works on the Favourites row of TV, Movies and TV Shows.

title: Clear channel history
answer: Asks first.

title: Catch-up playlists
answer: The Catch-up group lists every channel your provider marks with catch-up. OK or → on a playlist hides or shows its channels in this group only (for a provider that marks channels it doesn't really keep). Settings > Interface > Tabs can hide the whole group.

title: Jump to a playlist, or hide its groups here
answer: OK jumps to that playlist's groups. → on a playlist hides or shows all its groups in this tab only (its channels stay in Search and Favourites).

title: Resume the last channel
answer: What the "Hold > to resume" pill means. Works even with the pill turned off in Settings.

title: Refine the existing appearance
answer: Off by default and independent for each profile. Adds glossy panels, brighter reflections, bevelled edges and blur around focused controls. Uses more graphics resources. Keeps the same layout, theme colours, text sizes and remote navigation. Turn it off to restore the original finish.

title: Hide the resume reminder
answer: Turn off Show the "Hold > to resume" reminder. This hides the pill while a channel plays in the background. On Android, holding Right still resumes the last channel.

title: Lock touch controls
answer: Tap the full-screen video to show its controls, then tap the open padlock in the top bar. Video keeps playing while taps, swipes and Back are blocked. The closed padlock stays visible on the left: tap it once to unlock and restore the controls. The lock stays through rotation and episode changes, is hidden in picture-in-picture, and resets when you leave the player. Android system Home and volume controls remain available. TV boxes do not show this button.

title: Back to live
answer: While a catch-up replay plays full screen, select the gold LIVE button to return to the channel live. Fast-forwarding to the end of the replay also returns to live. It is not a guide shortcut: Back or Now in the guide only moves the guide to the current time and leaves the replay playing.

title: Watch a programme from the start
answer: To restart a programme on a catch-up-capable channel, open the player bar and choose Watch from the start, or open the Channel schedule and pick it. Your provider must offer that part of the programme.
controls: Android · player bar: Watch from the start

title: Skip back and forward
answer: In full screen, on a movie, an episode or a catch-up replay, each press skips 10 seconds like the -10 / +10 buttons; keep pressing or hold to skip further (up to 5 minutes a step). The video jumps once you stop. On a live channel with catch-up, Rewind goes back in minutes from now.

title: Pause live TV and resume
answer: You can pause live TV on a channel that supports catch-up, then press Play to resume from where you paused. Short pauses use the existing buffer; after more than 90 seconds VesperTV uses the provider's catch-up feed (timeshift). Availability still depends on the provider's replay window. Use the gold LIVE button in full screen when you want to return to live.
controls: Android catch-up channel · remote ⏯ or player Play/Pause

title: Seek and change replay programmes
answer: The catch-up player shows a CATCH-UP tag, programme progress and how far behind live you are. Use the time bar to seek within the programme, or the previous / next programme buttons when listings are available. Next returns to live if there is no later programme to replay. At the end of the programme you picked, playback pauses so the next one doesn't start on its own: press Play to carry on, or turn on Settings → Playback → Catch-up → Keep playing after the programme. A paused live channel resuming through catch-up keeps going until it catches up to live.
controls: Android replay · player bar: previous / restart / next · ↑ to the time bar

title: Side panel
answer: Last channels, My Teams and Live now, without leaving the video. OK on one switches to it; Back closes the panel. Phone: swipe right to open, swipe left to close.

title: Last channel
answer: Jumps back to the channel you watched before this one. Press → again to flip between the two. On movies and Media Hub titles, → still opens Stream sources.

title: Pull stats
answer: The game's box score and stats open beside the panel, over the video.
controls: Hold OK on a game in the side panel

title: Player bar + info card
answer: OK opens the player bar with Play/Pause selected (clock, transport, favourite). On a live channel the info card shows above it: what's on now and next, with a gold tag naming the channel's playlist. On a channel with a guide listing, a timeline shows the programme's start, end and how far it has gone; on a catch-up channel, Up from the buttons selects it and Left / Right go back into catch-up (it starts 0.7 s after your last press, or on OK; back to now returns to live). Six seconds without a key hides everything; Back hides it at once.

title: Change channel with the arrows
answer: With nothing on screen, Up and Down change channel like CH+ / CH− (handy on Fire TV remotes, which have no channel buttons). On movies and episodes they open the player bar.

title: Channel schedule
answer: With the player bar and info card up, Up highlights Channel schedule and OK opens the channel's programmes on the left, on the show playing. Rewind / Fast-forward on the remote jump a screenful. OK on a past show with catch-up watches it from the start; OK on the show on now goes back to live. OK on an upcoming show opens Remind me / Record. Reminders appear five minutes before and at the start while VesperTV is open; they never change the channel. Record uses the guide start and end times and can run while the app is closed (leave the box powered). Reopen the upcoming show to cancel, or manage recordings in Recordings. Back returns to the selected programme.

title: Skip intro / credits
answer: While the white Skip intro, Skip recap or Skip credits button shows, OK skips it. In the credits with another episode queued, it says Next episode and plays it. The button hides after 10 seconds and comes back when you bring up the player bar. Times come from IntroDB; turn it off in Settings › Playback › Skip intro.

title: Data pool
answer: Stream info in the options row opens the stream details card for 10 seconds: resolution, frame rate, codecs, measured bitrate, buffer and playback state. It's on by default; turn it off in Settings › Playback › Data pool to remove the tile.

title: More options
answer: Down from the player bar swaps it for a row of options: Channels list, Stream info, Recall, Watch from the start, Reload channel, Audio track, Subtitles, Audio sync, linked channel, Multiview, Sources, Fill screen and Search. Left / Right move along it, OK picks one, Up or Back returns to the player bar. Phones keep these buttons in the player bar.

title: Audio sync (audio delay)
answer: If the sound is ahead of or behind the picture, open Audio sync and press Right (sound later) or Left (sound earlier) in 25 ms steps (hold to go faster, up to 5 seconds either way); it changes as you press, so line it up by eye, then OK. Also in Settings › Playback › Audio › Audio delay. Applies to this device, every channel.

title: Next / previous channel
answer: Zaps through the list you opened the channel from. Page Up / Page Down do the same.

title: Scrub the time bar
answer: On a movie or episode, Up from the buttons selects the time bar. Hold Left or Right: the marker jumps further the longer you hold (10 s up to 5 min) and shows the target time. Let go and it seeks there; OK seeks at once. Down returns to the buttons. Smaller subtitles: Subtitles › Subtitle size › Extra small.

title: When the next episode starts
answer: 30 seconds before the end (default: the Up Next card counts down over the credits), When the episode ends, or Never (no countdown; the episode plays to its end). Applies to this device.
controls: Settings → Playback → Up Next EPISODE · ANDROID

title: Watch game
answer: With Settings → Sports Trak → Watch game button on, a game you set a reminder for offers a Watch game button in the player when it starts. It shows for 10 seconds, then only with the player bar, for 10 minutes. Up from the bar selects it; OK switches to the game on its best channel. It never changes the channel by itself.
controls: ↑ from the player bar, then OK ANDROID

title: Play / Pause
answer: The remote's own Play/Pause key works anywhere in the player.

title: Leave full screen
answer: With the side panel open, Back closes the panel first. On TV, Back first hides the player bar or the options row.

title: Choose a profile at startup
answer: Turn this on, then fully close and reopen VesperTV. After the splash, use the arrows and OK, or tap a profile, to open the app in that profile. The last-used profile starts focused. Photos appear when set; leaving a restricted profile still needs the PIN. The switch is off by default and applies to this device.
controls: Settings > General > Startup > Launch with profiles selector

title: Hide profiles on Home
answer: Turn this on to remove the profiles row from Home. It is off by default and applies to the active profile. You can still manage profiles in Settings.

title: Back to Who's watching
answer: With Settings > General > Startup > Launch with profiles selector enabled, leaving the TV or Sports Mode root stops playback and returns to Who's watching. In Sports Mode, first use Back to open the sidebar and stop its player. Back on Who's watching asks whether to exit, with Stay selected. With the startup selector off, the existing exit flow stays in place.
controls: TV home / Sports Mode root · Back

title: Favourite on / off
answer: A star appears on the poster, and the title joins Favourites.

title: Actor portraits and credits
answer: With a TMDB API key saved, Cast jumps to the portrait section. Press OK or Down to enter the actor row, Left/Right to browse and OK on an actor for their movie/show credits. Pick a credit to look for a matching title in your enabled IPTV playlists; a missing match is reported without opening another source. Back restores the actor card. Up returns through the section button to the movie actions or show episodes; on a portrait phone show page it returns to Play. Without a TMDB key, the existing floating cast names stay available. Metadata loads separately and does not block Play.
controls: OK on Cast in an IPTV movie or show page

title: Mark watched / unwatched
answer: A watched episode starts over from the beginning. Synced to Trakt / Simkl when signed in.
controls: Hold OK on a season chip to mark the whole season watched / unwatched; on an episode

title: Expand catalog
answer: The whole group as a grid, with sorting (and TMDB release-date sorting if you added a TMDB key).

title: Manage source cards
answer: Open from Settings › Media Hub › Media Hub sources, or Sources in the Media Hub tab. Add a source, From phone, Stremio import, Jellyfin / Emby and Trakt / Simkl are at the top. Playback sources provide video; Catalogs & lists, including Cinemeta, provide titles that play through those sources. Left/Right moves between cards; Up/Down moves through their controls and grid rows, scrolling as needed. OK on Enabled switches a source on or off; hold OK there to remove it. View source URL reveals the saved link and offers Copy URL. Show under Other puts an add-on behind the Other genre filter; refresh Media Hub after changing it.

title: Stream sources
answer: Slide out the other files for this movie or episode, including provider, advertised format and size when available. Up/Down browses, OK switches at the current position and saves the selected source for resume; Left or Back closes.

title: Left panel
answer: Search, Movies, TV Shows, Refresh, Media Hub sources and Jellyfin / Emby. Up/Down moves between these entries and stays at the ends; Right enters the title rows. While you browse the rows or the top bar it folds to a slim strip of icons; Left (or Back) from the rows opens it again and slides the rows aside. On a TV, the title you're on fills the top of the page with its logo, genre, year, IMDb rating and description, and its card turns into a wide picture after you keep it focused for two seconds. Rows scroll with each selection, keeping the selector near the left edge so you can see upcoming titles, until you reach the end of the row.

title: Search movies or TV shows
answer: A small menu slides out beside Search: pick Movies or TV Shows, then type. Results come first in the rows; the top bar shows Sources and a Clear button with your search. Phones keep Search in the top bar.
controls: OK on Search in the left panel

title: Floating bar
answer: Genre is first in the top menu, followed by Newest and the row buttons. On a phone, genres are first in Menu. Genre › Other holds add-on catalogs that aren't plain movies or series. Newest shows only this year's releases (from a source's release-year catalog, such as the New row); pick a genre as well to see the new releases in that genre. Sources whose titles carry no genre information drop out while a genre is picked. After adding a TMDB catalog to an add-on, press Refresh so Newest can use it.

title: Favourite on / off
answer: On Recently watched, hold removes the title from that row instead.

title: Row menu
answer: Expand catalog (the whole row as a grid) or Go to row.
controls: Hold OK on a row's bar button

title: Your source finished fetching it
answer: If a title played a short "being downloaded" video, press Back and carry on. The poster gets a Ready tag when the full file is there. Optional: add your debrid key in Settings › Media Hub › Debrid accounts for an exact check.

title: Mark watched / unwatched
answer: Same as provider shows.
controls: Hold OK on a season chip to mark the whole season watched / unwatched; on an episode

title: Sports Mode (beta)
answer: Enable it in Sports Trak or Settings → Sports Trak → Sports Mode to make sports your home for this profile. Your first five leagues sit in a sidebar; the rest, All and Edit leagues stay in the floating top bar. Left from the feed or the first card/control opens the sidebar; Right returns to the page. All opens a dropdown of every enabled league. Today opens the day picker. Standings, My Teams and Networks remain available. Menu gathers Home, Search, Multiview and the other app shortcuts. Turn Sports Mode off to restore the regular home and your previous startup choice. See the player, Live TV panel and Back controls below for the TV layout; narrow and touch layouts keep scrolling page controls.

title: Sports Mode big and small player
answer: On TV, the first game you play opens the big player beside the game feed. Up/Down browses the feed; OK previews a game and OK again on that playing game opens full screen. Right on a feed game also opens full screen; hold OK opens its stats. Down past the feed opens the card rows with a small player. OK on another card there changes the stream and keeps the small player and cards visible. Up from the first card row returns to the big player and feed. Back from full screen returns to the sports page.
controls: Sports Mode · ↓ past the feed · ↑ from the first card row

title: Sports Mode Live TV panel
answer: On TV layouts, Live TV opens groups and a translucent channel guide inside Sports Mode. OK on a group opens its guide. OK on a channel plays it in the Sports Mode player beside the guide; OK again on that channel opens full screen using the same stream. A game keeps playing while you browse, until you choose a channel. Back from full screen returns to the open guide with the channel still playing. With the guide closed, Right from a group moves into the sports page; with the guide open, Right enters that guide. Left from the page's left edge returns to the open panel. Back closes the channel guide, then the groups panel, returning to the sports page. CH+/CH- or Page Up/Page Down move eight rows. Open full Live TV opens the regular TV screen; narrow and touch layouts use that screen directly.
controls: Sports Mode · Live TV or Guide / EPG

title: Sports Mode Back chain
answer: From the sports page, Back opens the sidebar and keeps the player running. Back on the sidebar stops playback; another Back leaves the sports root. With Launch with profiles selector enabled, it returns to Who's watching; otherwise it asks to exit. If a Live TV panel is open, Back first closes its channel guide, then its groups panel. Back while reordering a league finishes the move. Regular Sports Trak keeps its existing Back behavior.
controls: Sports Mode · Back on the page, then on the sidebar

title: Choose the best quality copy
answer: On by default, per profile. Offers a matched 4K game source first, even from a different broadcaster; your explicit channel pick always wins. Turn it off to use the usual match order. Returning to Sports Trak applies the choice to the current games.
controls: Settings → Sports Trak → Prefer highest quality

title: Preview, then full screen
answer: Focusing a game updates the big matchup and its key stats. Press OK or tap once to preview its matched channel; press again on the same playing game for full screen using the same stream. In the Sports Mode TV layout, the first game opens the big player beside the feed; while browsing card rows, another card plays in the small player. Regular Sports Trak uses its mini player. With no matched channel, the game menu opens to choose one. Hold keeps the existing menu. Live and finished games show available leaders, latest play/goal and team stats; upcoming games show standings on each team's side with injuries in the middle. Hide scores also hides result-revealing stats.

title: Watch in the hero
answer: Starts or stops the game's channel in the sports player. OK on the playing game goes full screen. In regular Sports Trak, Back stops the preview. Sports Mode uses the Back chain below.

title: Game menu
answer: Play here, choose another channel, Record until the show ends / until I stop it (Android).

title: Reorder leagues
answer: The league strip uses short labels such as AHL, EPL, UCL and F1; Edit leagues keeps the full names. In the Sports Mode sidebar, move the league with ↑ ↓. Top-row leagues, narrow horizontal strips and regular Sports Trak use ← →. Moving across the fifth slot transfers a league between the sidebar and top row. OK or Back finishes the move.
controls: Hold OK on a league chip

title: Your leagues
answer: Sports Mode shows a dropdown arrow: press OK or click All to open it. Hold OK also opens the menu in Sports Mode and regular Sports Trak. Every enabled league is listed, including sidebar leagues, off-screen top-row leagues and those with no games, with the day’s game/live counts. Pick a league to filter, or choose All leagues at the top to clear the filter. You do not need to hide another league to select one.
controls: OK on All ▾ in Sports Mode · Hold OK on All

title: Pick its channel
answer: NFL Sundays.
controls: Hold OK on the RedZone pill

title: Live games list
answer: Every live game in one list. OK = stats pop-up, Hold OK = channel menu, ⏯ = play full screen.

title: Follow it (My Teams)
answer: Followed teams' games come first, with a star.
controls: OK on a team in Standings

title: Remind me
answer: Choose Remind me to open the timing menu: 15 minutes, 1 hour, 1 day or 1 week before, plus a reminder at game time. You can also choose At game time only. Passed advance times are unavailable. Popups appear above any screen or stream while VesperTV is open. You do not need to follow either team. For teams in My Teams, choose Remind me for every game to enable automatic reminders for that team, or Stop team reminders to disable them. Hold again to Cancel reminder for one game, or choose Reminder timing to change its advance time. Automatic team reminders keep the 15-minute default unless you override an individual game. A faded team logo appears behind the popup text. Reminders belong to the current viewer on this device.
controls: Hold OK on any upcoming Sports Trak game

title: Score alerts for one match
answer: Choose Set goals alert for this match to get the existing top-left score popup when either team scores, even if neither team is in My Teams. Remove goals alert for this match stops it. This per-game choice works independently of the My Teams Goals alert switch. Hide scores still pauses in-app score popups. Choices belong to this profile and device; alerts follow the sports feed while VesperTV is open.
controls: Hold OK on an upcoming or live team game

title: Score alerts for a whole league
answer: Choose Goals alert for all of (league) to get the score popup for every goal in that league, for any team. Remove goals alert for (league) stops it. Hide scores pauses these alerts too. Saved for this profile on this device.
controls: Hold OK on a game, or on a league in League manager

title: Game and goal notifications on Android
answer: Game reminders and Goal alerts are on by default for this viewer; they notify only for reminders and goals you subscribed to. Reminders use the saved advance time and kickoff time even after normal app closure. My Teams goal alerts and per-match goal alerts use one ongoing Following goals notification during scheduled games, with a Stop action. Each game is limited to five hours. Tap an alert to open its game in Sports Trak. While the app is visible, its existing popups take over. Hide scores removes score text from system goal notifications. Android notification permission and exact-alarm access are needed; Force stop prevents delivery until you reopen the app, and power-saving restrictions or delayed sports feeds can delay alerts.

title: Prefer channels from your country
answer: Select one or more countries with equal priority. Canadian preferences recognize TSN, Sportsnet, RDS and TVA Sports, including untagged channel names. Country tags and your manual Country corrections help identify other feeds. Explicit game/team picks stay first; game-name or guide evidence stays ahead of generic broadcaster suggestions. Among comparable matches, a preferred playlist comes first when set, then preferred countries, with your usual quality preference inside each group. Other countries remain available as fallbacks. No country preference ranks all countries equally; a playlist preference still applies. Choices belong to this viewer and travel in Backup and Transfer.
controls: Settings → Sports Trak → Preferred channel countries

title: Prefer matching channels from one playlist
answer: Choose an enabled playlist to prefer its matching channels before country and video quality among comparable matches. Your saved game/team channel choices and manually added sources stay first; game-name or guide evidence stays ahead of generic broadcaster suggestions. Other playlists remain available when the preferred one has no suitable match. Disabled or hidden channels are never enabled by this setting. No playlist preference removes this priority while keeping your country choices. Saved for this viewer; included in Backup, Transfer and copying Main's Sports settings.

title: Hide quiet leagues for the selected day
answer: Off by default. Turn it on to hide leagues whose schedules confirm there are no games on the day shown. Changing the day updates the league row and Sports Mode sidebar/top row. Upcoming, live and finished games all count, including live games continuing past midnight. Loading or unavailable schedules do not establish an empty league. Your saved league order and favourite are kept; Edit leagues still contains every saved league. If the selected league has no games, the view returns to All. Turning the setting off restores the complete league navigation. Saved for this viewer and included in Backup, Transfer and copying Main's Sports settings.
controls: Settings → Sports Trak → Hide leagues with no games

title: Show betting odds
answer: Off by default. Turn it on to see the line and over/under at the bottom of upcoming and live game cards, in the middle of the matchup panel when there is no injury to show, and a full table (moneyline, spread, total, and draw for soccer) at the top of the game stats (hold OK, Stats). Odds come with the scores from one sportsbook, mostly for North American leagues; finished games show none. Display only: the app never takes bets or links to a sportsbook. Saved for this viewer.

title: Score alerts for My Teams
answer: Off by default. Enable it for a top-left popup when any followed team scores, above any screen or stream while VesperTV is open. The card shows the team and league logos, the current score and, when the sports feed has it, who scored. Game reminders stay top-right; on a phone the cards stack. Alerts follow the sports feed's update speed, pause with Hide scores or when the app is in the background, and do not replay old scores on launch or profile changes.

title: Schedule, Follow, Unfollow or preferred channel
answer: In My Teams, Set preferred channel opens your visible live channels, with search and playlist groups. Choose one to use it by default for that team in this league, even when no upcoming game is listed. Automatic channel removes the team preference. An explicitly chosen channel for one match still wins. Hidden or unavailable channels are not played. Choices belong to this viewer. Schedule opens the team's season as a month calendar: each game day shows the opponent's logo and the time or result. Football (soccer) includes the cups (FA Cup, Carabao Cup, Champions League…), marked with the cup's logo. Arrows move a day or a week, CH+/CH- change month. OK shows the stats of a finished game, watches a live one or opens the game menu of an upcoming one (reminder, record, channel); hold OK opens the game menu.
controls: Hold OK on a team in Standings or My Teams

title: Show / hide, favourite, send back
answer: Your leagues stay on the left; the league bank is on the right (below on phones). In the bank, OK expands or collapses a sport: Football 🏈, Football ⚽, Hockey 🏒 and more. Up/Down moves through sport headings and expanded leagues, scrolling the selector into view in either direction. Left/Right switches columns and remembers your place. OK on a bank league adds it and keeps the selector in the bank. OK on one of your leagues shows or hides it in the tab. Hold: Make favourite league (Sports Trak opens on it), Send back to the league bank.

title: Move the sound
answer: The speaker dot shows which screen you hear.

title: Screen menu
answer: Full screen, Reload, Change channel and Remove. In Android 1 + 3, a small screen also offers Move to the big screen, and Swap mode is available from the hold menu or header. The menu scrolls when needed.

title: Swap mode
answer: In the 1 + 3 layout, start Swap mode to rotate the playing screens through the big screen with the arrows. Streams keep playing without reconnecting, and sound follows the big screen. A blinking SWAP label beneath it and a brief flash mark each change. OK or Back finishes swapping. Windows keeps its existing 2- and 4-screen layouts.
controls: Android · 1 + 3 · Hold OK → Swap mode, or the header button

title: Header
answer: The layout switch and Multiview's other buttons. Android in landscape offers 2 screens, 4 screens, or 1 + 3: one big screen with three small ones. Windows keeps the 2- and 4-screen layouts. ↓ goes back to the screens.

title: Show the controls
answer: The first OK only brings back the name and back arrow. Back always works.

title: Recording menu
answer: While it records: Watch live, Play from the start, Stop recording (keeps it), Cancel recording.

title: Vesper AI
answer: Vesper AI is the voice and typed-command assistant in Android 1.0.59+. Built-in commands are free, with no AI account or API key. Select the Vesper row in the side menu, the microphone in Search, or Talk to Vesper now in Settings. In the panel, choose Talk, type in Or type here, or choose Talk from my phone. Vesper shortcut in Settings shows or hides the menu shortcut. This is available in Android 1.0.59 and later; the public Windows download remains 1.0.45.
controls: Open Vesper AI: menu Vesper · Search microphone · Settings → Vesper AI → Talk to Vesper now

title: Vesper AI without an API key
answer: Built-in commands are free and parsed on your device: try "play TSN 1", "mets RDS", "pause", "next channel", "what's on TSN 1", "when is the Simpsons on", "today's games", "put on the Habs game", "search for Dune" or "help". The channel, programme or game must be available in your own sources and guide. Going back on live TV needs provider catch-up support. Leave Your AI set to None to use built-in commands only. Local command parsing does not make streaming, guide updates or voice recognition work offline.
controls: Type or say: play TSN 1 · pause · go back 30 seconds · today's games · help

title: Talk to Vesper AI from your phone
answer: Open Talk from my phone in the Vesper panel or Settings → Vesper AI. Scan the QR code with your phone and leave VesperTV open on the TV. For the same-Wi-Fi page, type or use the microphone on your phone's keyboard; that HTTP page has no browser microphone button. When AI apps are enabled, the QR page can use the internet relay instead; its own microphone button depends on browser support and microphone permission. Keep the phone link private. The same-Wi-Fi keyboard microphone is an alternative when the TV remote microphone is unavailable; the off-network relay phone path still needs real-device testing.
controls: Talk from my phone → scan the QR code → type or use the phone keyboard microphone

title: Vesper AI remote voice button
answer: The remote voice-button option is off by default. Turn it on, or use Teach it your remote's button and press the button you want Vesper to learn. Android must deliver that key to the app, and the device needs a working speech-recognition service and microphone permission. Fire TV keeps its Alexa button for the system, so use Talk from my phone or type instead. Teaching cannot capture a key the system never sends. Remote microphone support has not been verified across TV boxes. Read replies aloud is a separate optional setting.
controls: Settings → Vesper AI → Remote voice button opens Vesper → Teach it your remote's button

title: Bring your own AI to Vesper
answer: For requests beyond built-in phrases, choose Claude, OpenAI-compatible or Gemini under Your AI, enter the provider's model and API key, then Save and test. OpenAI-compatible services also use the Address field; a local compatible server can run without a key. Key from phone avoids typing a key with the remote. Vesper tries built-in commands first; an unrecognized request or failed built-in command can then go to your configured AI. API usage is billed by your chosen provider where applicable, separately from VesperTV. These provider integrations still need real-account testing; built-in commands remain available without them.
controls: Settings → Vesper AI → Your AI → provider, model and API key → Save and test

title: Connect an AI app with MCP
answer: Enable Let AI apps control VesperTV and copy this TV's private connector address into a compatible AI app's custom MCP connector. A Claude connector was tested; other clients, including ChatGPT, still need testing and must support custom MCP connections. Leave VesperTV open on that TV. Ask on the TV first is on by default: starting a channel or title, hiding/showing groups and clearing the watch list wait for confirmation. Read-only requests, player controls and individual list edits can run without a dialog. The address itself grants access: keep it private. Reset the address invalidates the old link; add the new address in your AI app. Disable Let AI apps control VesperTV to stop remote requests.
controls: Settings → Vesper AI → AI apps → Let AI apps control VesperTV

title: Vesper AI on several TVs
answer: Each TV has its own connector address. Add a separate connector for each TV and name them clearly in your AI app, for example VesperTV Living room and VesperTV Bedroom. The link targets that one TV; Vesper does not yet offer a shared multi-TV link or choose a TV automatically. Keep the intended TV's VesperTV app open.
controls: One private connector address per TV

title: Vesper AI watch list
answer: Ask Vesper to "add this to my watch list", add an available title by name, or show your watch list. A linked AI app can also add available titles with a note, for example a list for Friday. Saved items appear in the Watch list row on Home for this viewer. Hold OK on a title there to remove it. This is VesperTV's own list, separate from Trakt or Simkl watchlists; it does not download video or add a new content source.
controls: Say: add this to my watch list · show my watch list · Home → Watch list → Hold OK

title: Vesper AI privacy
answer: With Your AI set to None, typed commands are handled without an AI provider. When enabled, Your AI can handle unrecognized requests and failed built-in commands. Your AI sends your request, conversation and tool results, such as channel/title names, programme listings, group names and watch-list notes, directly from the TV to your chosen AI provider. They do not pass through the VesperTV relay. A linked MCP app receives tool replies through the relay; the relay phone page also carries requests through that link. Relay requests and replies wait temporarily in memory, with no saved conversation history. Your AI provider or connected app has its own data policies. Voice recognition follows the TV or phone speech service's behavior; local command parsing is not a promise of local-only speech processing.
controls: Built-in commands · Your AI · AI apps over the relay

title: Vesper AI limits and Windows
answer: Vesper acts on the sources and guide you already have. Its search/play tools cover your IPTV channels, movies and shows; Media Hub search through the AI tools and picking an episode by command are not implemented. A series opens its show page so you can choose the episode. Hidden content, restricted viewer permissions and Hide scores still apply. The public Windows package is 1.0.45 and does not include Vesper AI; the merged Windows code has not had real UI testing, and voice, player controls and now-playing support are not available there yet.
controls: Your IPTV sources and guide · select episodes on the show page

title: Use a channel logo from your EPG
answer: Open the editor on your phone or PC. In a channel's Guide popup, choose Main guide or an Extra guide, search for the channel and select Use EPG logo beside its preview. Save changes to apply the image. Link changes programme matching separately. Use provider logo resets only the image. If the directory is empty after starting VesperTV, choose Update EPG Now, then search again when it finishes. Your chosen logo URL is saved for this viewer and playlist, survives content updates and travels in Backup and Transfer. Later changes to the guide's logo URL require selecting it again.
controls: Settings → Playlists & guide → Playlist editor → Guide and logo

title: Filter Group Management
answer: TV, Movies and TV Shows each have their own search. Type US to show groups starting with US; the list narrows with each letter. Show results / Hide results affects only those matches. Clear search restores every group. The keyboard's Search key moves to Show results, or Clear search if there are no matches.

title: In and out of a category
Type
answer: The keyboard only opens on OK, so the arrows can pass over a text box. On a Fire TV the on-screen keyboard keeps the Back key for itself; use its own close or Done key.

title: On / off, or remove
answer: Settings › Media Hub › Add-ons. In Media Hub sources, use the Enabled control inside a source card.
controls: OK / Hold OK on an add-on

title: Set up sync without an account
answer: Sync is planned for an upcoming release; it is not in public Android 1.0.56 or Windows 1.0.45 yet. Open Sync on your first device and choose Set up sync. No account, email or login is needed. Save the recovery code shown once, then choose I saved my recovery code. Your setup is encrypted on the device; the server stores only ciphertext and cannot read it.
controls: Settings > Device & data > Sync > Set up sync

title: Link another device to sync
answer: On an already linked device, choose Link a device. Enter its 16-digit link code under I have a code on the other device; the QR contains the same code as text. Each link code is single-use: it works once, for one device, and expires after 10 minutes. Its first download uses it up. Create a new link code for each additional device; an expired or already used code needs a new one. Use the Sync code screen, not Transfer > Receive. All link codes and the recovery code share the same limit of 3 devices per sync; another code does not reset that count. If both devices already have the same server and username or M3U URL, sync matches that playlist so favourites and watch positions line up.
controls: Sync > Link a device; other device > I have a code

title: What syncs between devices
answer: Playlists, viewer profiles, favourites and their order, hidden groups and channels, own groups, watch positions, recently played / Continue Watching lists, Sports Trak preferences, Media Hub sources/favourites/resume/history and shared settings sync. Layout, enabled playlists on this box, playlist/guide caches, current viewer, PIN lockout and backup timers stay on this device. Profile photos and imported M3U files do not sync in this first version. Continue Watching and Media Hub Recently watched merge newest first. Sync copies your setup, not channels or video files.

title: Sync now and last sync time
answer: Last sync shows the time of the latest successful sync; Sync now requests another round. Check the error message if it cannot reach the server. Linked devices also sync while VesperTV is open and when it returns to the screen. Some setup and settings changes appear after a full restart. The first join of an existing playlist can also wait until restart to keep its identity and favourites together.

title: Show or use a sync recovery code
answer: The recovery code has 26 characters, displayed in groups with dashes, plus a QR. Show recovery code asks for the profile PIN when one is set. On the new device choose I have a code, then Use a recovery code, and enter it. Keep this code private: anyone holding it can join your sync. A 16-digit link code works once for one device; the recovery code is the lasting way back in. Both use the same 3-device limit for that sync.
controls: Sync > Show recovery code; other device > I have a code > Use a recovery code

title: Lost sync recovery code
answer: If you lost the recovery code but still have a linked device, open Sync > Show recovery code there (profile PIN when set). If you lose all linked devices and the recovery code, we cannot recover your old sync. Set up a new sync from the data you still have. No email or account can restore the old code.
controls: Keep a linked device or the saved recovery code

title: Reset the sync code
answer: Reset sync code asks for the profile PIN when set, then confirmation. Reset removes all your encrypted data from the old server copy and clears its device slots. This device keeps its local data and starts a new sync. Save the new recovery code. Every other device stops syncing and must be linked again using a new link code or the new recovery code. Only a small reset notice remains for 30 days so offline devices can learn of the reset; the old snapshot cannot be uploaded again during that period. Use reset if a code was shared accidentally or a linked box was sold.

title: Stop syncing on this device
answer: Confirm Stop syncing on this device to unlink only this device. Your local setup stays, and other devices keep syncing. If this device can reach the server, stopping also frees its place among the 3 devices. This is different from Reset sync code, which requires other devices to link again.
controls: Sync > Stop syncing on this device

title: Sync deleted after three months
answer: The server deletes a sync after 3 months (90 days) without any linked device checking in. Using a linked device refreshes that period. The temporary 16-digit link code still expires after 10 minutes. After server expiry, a device with the recovery code can start that sync again from its remaining local data; the deleted server snapshot cannot be recovered.
controls: No device checks in for 3 months

title: Sync device limit: 3 devices
answer: Each sync supports 3 devices in total. Link codes and the recovery code all lead to the same sync, so generating another code does not reset the count. If you see “This sync already has 3 devices”, open Sync on one linked device and choose Stop syncing on this device, then try linking again. A device unused for 30 days frees its place automatically. A device returning after losing its place needs to link again if the sync is full.
controls: Sync > Stop syncing on one linked device

title: Select, then open
answer: One click selects a poster or channel (and fills the banner), a second click opens it.

title: Hold menus
answer: Holding the mouse button opens the same menus as Hold OK.

title: Mute
answer: The volume slider sits in the player bar and is remembered.

title: Side panel
answer: Same as on a TV, when the player bar isn't selected.
